title: Buddy Petit, Kid Rena and Chris Kelly; their influence
summary: Albert recalls visiting Buddy Petit in a one-room shack and praises him, Kid Rena and Chris Kelly, whose plunger work Cootie Williams took. He compares Punch Miller, Billy Douglas and Louis.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I can remember the trees and the green shrubbery. A few homes. Beautiful homes sitting in these, under these great big trees. Of course, you had the slum area over there. Well, now I wouldn't say slum. I hate to use it. Yeah. But, for instance, Buddy B.T. lived in the great trumpet players about 25, 30 years ahead of time. He lived in the little one room shack and he took a vacuum to me. And every time I would go to the dock, I'd try to see how fast I could get off of that. And we'd sit down and talk with Buddy. And I'd ask him questions about his horn. And I thought all in all he was a grandfellow. Too bad that there's not too much on the record to preserve what he really done. A lot of credit goes to Buddy B.T. And a lot of credit goes to Buddy B.T. And he deserves it. And people like Buddy B.T. and Kip Renee. And another one that I most certainly have to mention because he was the most beautiful trumpet player and blues player I've ever heard in my life was Chris Kelly. And if you ever listen to Cootie Williams with Duke when Cootie plays with the plunger, Cootie picked this up from Chris Kelly. Well that's one of the things that I wanted to talk to you about.
One of the things I was trying to get in there from a slant and vicular way as a country.
Like you go over there and you hear Buddy. Is there anybody on the record that sounds like Buddy that you've ever heard?

Not that I can recall right now. But I tell you what. Punch Miller, when Punch was young, he copied Buddy B.T. style as close as he could. But today, no I can't say that I, well, if you listen to my records, you'll hear a trumpet player named Billy Douglas. I think Billy Douglas is one of the greatest trumpet players I've ever heard in my life. Technical. The tonation wasn't the best in the world, but as a technical trumpet player, making things that we musicians hear are almost impossible, you get a vivid idea of what I'm trying to say about Punch and about Buddy. It was a variation style that these guys played. Well then you come along with Louis, and now you have a different vein all together. Louis didn't fingers harm too much as people say, on certain numbers, yes. But his mostly was from what he felt within himself, which made quite a difference. That's the difference in musicians playing music today, and musicians playing music in the olden days. Well, a lot of people say you're old-timing. Well, maybe I am old-timing. But the fact still remains within me such that if I listen to something, I want to enjoy it. And these guys brought out of their souls on their instruments, looking at you and you looking at them, and it was communication there of happiness. Which today I imagine to some people is happiness, but I don't see too much happiness when I look in the crowd.
